title: Dark patterns
summary: A clean, fast take: no "scratch that", no pause over 1.2 s, first word at 0.08 s. Only one restart and the trailing "I don't know." at the end.

cuts.why: "Depending on where you live," then she restarts: "not a lawyer, but depending on where you live and everything that I read and studied…". Keeps the second.
Cuts the trailing "I don't know." so the video ends on "We can make the world a better place." Also removes the room tone after it.

decisions:
- **Ending (cut 2)**: if she likes the throwaway "I don't know." as her style, skip it and cut only from 460.78 to the end.
- **7:30 "I genuinely don't think users have to consistently... Like, users have been manipulated in different places."**: an unfinished sentence just before the end; she may want to cut 7:30.0 to 7:37.7 too so it goes "…try to build the honest version. We can make the world a better place." (check by ear).
- **4:33 "something called an A and B testing, A/B testing"**: a small self-correction in fast speech, no clean gap; left in.
- **3:24 "I think Snapchat does this to me a lot"**: names a real app from her own experience. Fine as her opinion; just noting it, since the kit kept examples generic.
- **6:44 "FTC"**: whisper wrote "FCC"; the kit (and the case) is the FTC. Fixed in the transcript; listen that she says FTC.
kit:
**Skipped from the kit:**
- Amazon settled "without admitting any wrongdoing" (on-screen card can carry it).
- The whole FTC "click to cancel" story (rule made in 2024, thrown out by a US court in July 2025, restarted March 2026, no new rule as of October 2026).
- "this is where things stand as of October 2026" (dates for the Digital Fairness Act status).
- The ICPEN/GPEN detail "including the FTC" and the exact 642 (she says "over 600 websites").

**Added:** her own stories ("This happens to me a lot" for hidden costs; "They literally charged me for a year's subscription"; Snapchat notifications "I'm this close to deleting the app"); the A/B testing section is longer and more opinionated; the advice for designers "Don't even try to say 'this is wrong' … just be like, 'Hey guys, we could be sued for this'".

**Facts to check:**
- 5:35 "In July 2024 … about 26 countries … over 600 websites … 76% … nearly 67% used more than one": ✓ kit (642 sites; ICPEN/GPEN). The 67% figure isn't in the kit; it matches the published sweep, but check the source before it goes on screen.
- 5:15 European Commission sweep January 2023: 399 shops, 148 with at least one of three, 42 fake countdown timers ✓ kit; "70 of them were hiding important information" is not in the kit (it matches the Commission's press release; check).
- 6:02 Unfair Commercial Practices Directive 2005 ✓; GDPR "a pre-ticked box does not count as consent" ✓; EU consumer law refund for pre-ticked extras ✓.
- 6:48 Amazon $2.5 billion, September 2025 ✓ kit.
- 6:59 Digital Fairness Act "hasn't been published yet" ✓ as of October 2026; date-sensitive.
- 0:37 Harry Brignull coined "dark patterns" in 2010 ✓.
